```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", message = FALSE, fig.width = 8,
                      fig.height = 3.6, out.width = "100%", dpi = 96, fig.retina = 2)
do.call(knitr::read_chunk, list("helpers.R"))
```

```{r longFormat, include = FALSE}
```

```{r style, include = FALSE}
```

Forward sensitivities of the decay chain, the derivatives of the states in the initial values
and parameters, of first and second order, and their seeding by a tangent. The generated code
evaluates the right-hand side on dual numbers, the sensitivities are integrated together with the
states ([Forward sensitivities](methods-forward.html)).

```{r library}
library(cppDE)
library(ggplot2)
```

## Model definition

`deriv = TRUE` (default of [`cppODE()`](../reference/cppODE.html)) builds first-order
sensitivities in every state and parameter not named in `fixed`. `deriv2 = TRUE`, or
`derivMode = "forward-forward"`, adds the second order; `deriv = FALSE` builds the states alone.

```{r models}
eqns  <- c(A = "-k1*A", B = "k1*A - k2*B")
parms <- c(A = 1, B = 0, k1 = 0.5, k2 = 0.2)
times <- seq(0, 10, by = 0.1)

chain  <- cppODE(eqns, modelname = "g3_chain", compile = FALSE)
rates  <- cppODE(eqns, fixed = c("A", "B"), modelname = "g3_rates", compile = FALSE)
plain  <- cppODE(eqns, deriv = FALSE, modelname = "g3_plain", compile = FALSE)
chain2 <- cppODE(eqns, deriv2 = TRUE, modelname = "g3_chain2", compile = FALSE)

compile(chain, rates, plain, chain2, output = "guide3", cores = 2)
attr(chain, "dimNames")$sens
attr(rates, "dimNames")$sens
```

## First-order sensitivities

`$tangent` has the dimensions `[time, state, sensitivity]`; the entry `[t, i, j]` is
$\partial x_i(t)/\partial \theta_j$.

```{r first-order}
out <- solveODE(chain, times, parms)
dim(out$tangent)
out$tangent[101, , ]
```

`fixed` of `solveODE()` holds sensitivities fixed in one call, without recompiling; `fixed` of
`cppODE()` leaves them out of the generated code.

```{r fixed}
dimnames(solveODE(chain, times, parms, fixed = c("A", "B"))$tangent)$sens
```

## Reparametrization by a tangent

`tangent` of [`solveODE()`](../reference/solveODE.html) is the Jacobian $\partial(x_0, p)/\partial\theta$
of a reparametrization. The result is then $\partial x/\partial\theta$, one column per direction,
and the cost grows with the number of columns. Three shapes are told apart by the rows:

| rows | meaning |
|:--|:--|
| a subset of states and parameters, by name | partial: the missing rows are zero |
| all states and parameters, states first | full: the whole Jacobian of the reparametrization |
| the states only | state-only: the parameter rows are the identity on the sensitivities |

A partial tangent with the unit vectors of `k1` and `k2` gives the reduced sensitivities, a single
column a directional derivative.

```{r partial}
S <- diag(2)
dimnames(S) <- list(c("k1", "k2"), c("k1", "k2"))
solveODE(chain, times, parms, tangent = S)$tangent[101, , ]

v <- matrix(c(1, -1), 2, dimnames = list(c("k1", "k2"), "k1 - k2"))
solveODE(chain, times, parms, tangent = v)$tangent[101, , "k1 - k2"]
out$tangent[101, , "k1"] - out$tangent[101, , "k2"]
```

The two directional results agree to the integration tolerance: the step grid follows the
tangent, see [`sensErrCon`](#error-control).

A full tangent of the rate constants on the log scale, $k_i = e^{\theta_i}$, has the column
$\partial k_i/\partial \theta_i = k_i$.

```{r log-scale, fig.height = 3}
Tlog <- rbind(matrix(0, 2, 2), diag(parms[c("k1", "k2")]))
dimnames(Tlog) <- list(names(parms), c("log_k1", "log_k2"))
outL <- solveODE(chain, times, parms, tangent = Tlog)

ggplot(longFormat(outL, "B"), aes(time, value)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~panel, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_continuous(n.breaks = 3)
```

A state-only tangent is the shape of `out$tangent[t, , ]`, so one solve continues another,
sensitivities included. The chain is autonomous, so two solves over five time units agree with one over
ten to the integration tolerance.

```{r continue}
first <- solveODE(chain, seq(0, 5, by = 0.1), parms)
x5    <- first$variable[51, ]
then  <- solveODE(chain, seq(0, 5, by = 0.1), c(x5, parms[c("k1", "k2")]),
                  tangent = first$tangent[51, , ])
max(abs(then$tangent[51, , ] - out$tangent[101, , ]))
```

## Solving without sensitivities

A model built with `deriv = FALSE` returns states and diagnostics only.

```{r plain}
outV <- solveODE(plain, times, parms)
names(outV)
max(abs(outV$variable - out$variable))
```

## Error control of the sensitivities {#error-control}

With `sensErrCon = TRUE` (default) the sensitivities enter the error test and the first step, so
they are resolved to the tolerance like the states. `sensErrCon = FALSE` takes the steps of a
value run: cheaper, less accurate, and the sensitivities are the exact derivative of the computed
solution, as in the [reverse mode](guide-reverse.html).

```{r sens-err-con}
ref <- solveODE(chain, times, parms, abstol = 1e-12, reltol = 1e-12)
off <- solveODE(chain, times, parms, sensErrCon = FALSE)
c(on = out$diagnostics$accepted, off = off$diagnostics$accepted,
  value = outV$diagnostics$accepted)
c(on = max(abs(out$tangent - ref$tangent)), off = max(abs(off$tangent - ref$tangent)))
```

## Second-order sensitivities

A model built with `deriv2 = TRUE` returns `$hessian`, `[time, state, sensitivity, sensitivity]`,
the second derivatives of every state.

```{r second-order}
out2 <- solveODE(chain2, times, parms)
dim(out2$hessian)
out2$hessian[101, "B", , ]
```

`hessian` of `solveODE()` is the second derivative of the reparametrization, with the rows of
`tangent` and two dimensions of directions; the default treats the inputs as affine in $\theta$.
On the log scale $\partial^2 k_i/\partial\theta_i^2 = k_i$:

```{r log-hessian}
Hlog <- array(0, c(4, 2, 2), dimnames = c(dimnames(Tlog), list(colnames(Tlog))))
Hlog["k1", "log_k1", "log_k1"] <- parms["k1"]
Hlog["k2", "log_k2", "log_k2"] <- parms["k2"]
solveODE(chain2, times, parms, tangent = Tlog, hessian = Hlog)$hessian[101, "B", , ]
```

The diagonal agrees to the integration tolerance with
$k_i^2\,\partial^2 B/\partial k_i^2 + k_i\,\partial B/\partial k_i$ from the plain Hessian:

```{r log-hessian-check}
k <- parms[c("k1", "k2")]
k^2 * diag(out2$hessian[101, "B", c("k1", "k2"), c("k1", "k2")]) +
  k * out2$tangent[101, "B", c("k1", "k2")]
```

The Hessian of one objective in many parameters is cheaper by forward over reverse
([chapter 4](guide-reverse.html)).
